RagShortTexts: Swiss forest freemen armed with cleaving halberds defended Alpine defiles against feudal.

Variants.Content: Dwelling around Lake Lucerne, the forest cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden guarded Alpine passes under imperial immediacy. Free mountain cattlemen mastered the eight-foot Swiss halberd, integrating an axe head, thrusting pike point, and rear grappling hook to pull armored lords from saddles.

Controlling the St. Gotthard route, Swiss leagues fiercely resisted Habsburg feudal domination. Fighting with absolute refusal to give quarter or ransom noble captives, their defile ambushes crushed knightly hosts.
Mountain halberds are forged from tough Alpine ore. Descending with two-handed leverage in a rocky gorge, a single chop can cleave through mail coif and clavicle in one stroke.
